1.why: 11 is the exact sum of two other options (5 + 6) while 30 is their product and 15 a half of it, the classic parts/product/sum bait ring around a sum key.

2.why: 5/14 is the hub of a plus-or-minus-one lattice: 6/14 is numerator+1, 5/13 denominator-1, 6/15 both+1, and 1/3 is exactly 5/15, denominator+1.

3.why: Two 3:4 pairs (21,28) and (36,48) plus lone 63; a key normally sits inside a scaled pair, so 63 reads as the odd generator and I take one pair member arbitrarily.

4.why: x<3 is the single value all four others derive from by one error each: sign flip, inequality flip, both, and x<7 as the un-completed final step.

5.why: 7 anchors the halving pair with 3.5 and 4.75 is the lone unhalvable form (bait), but 12/24 is an equally good pair so this is not decidable.

6.why: 189, 210, 231 is a three-term arithmetic run of difference 21 with 210 at the middle and 240/330 as outliers.

7.why: 15 is the derivational hub: 15/7, 7.5=15/2, 5=15/3 and 3=15/5 are all quotients of it, so every distractor is generated from 15.

8.why: 1.8, 18 and 18000 are one decimal-shift family and 18 is the central placement; 30 and 13.5 are unrelated outliers.

9.why: 52 generates 10.4 (=52/5) and 8.67 (=52/6) as averaging quotients, but 12 and 18.4 stay unexplained so the hub covers only half the set.

10.why: 125 is the hub: 25=125/5, 750=125x6 and 3375=125x27 all derive from it, and 30 is just 25+5 noise.

11.why: 12.96, 21.6, [36], 60, 100 is a x5/3 geometric chain with no complete printed triple, so I take the round central member 60.

12.why: 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 is a three-term arithmetic run of difference 1/8 with 3/8 at the middle; 1/12 and the improper 17/12 are the add/subtract outliers.

13.why: 243/729/6561 are powers of 3 with 729 central and 83 the alien, but no complete geometric triple is printed so the middle is not forced.

14.why: No run, no sum, no hub: 90 is a lone round total and 29/19/15/20 are unstructured, so this is an unforced pick.

15.why: 2.5 and 0.4 are exact reciprocals (the inverted-ratio pair) and I bet on the non-fractional member, but the direction inside the pair is a coin toss.

16.why: 24, 48, 96, 192 is a four-term doubling chain so both 48 and 96 are middles; 32 is the outlier and I take the lower-central 48.

17.why: 64 is both the middle of the arithmetic run 62, 64, 66 and the only perfect square/power of two in the set; two rules converge.

18.why: 42/84 and 45/90 are two doubling pairs with 54 unpaired; a key usually carries its own doubling bait, so I take a pair member but cannot tell which.

19.why: 15 with 30 present is the combinations-versus-permutations shape (didn't-halve bait), which I bet on over the 30-as-hub reading; 1, 4, 6 are small-count noise.

20.why: 25 is the middle of the arithmetic run 23, 25, 27 and is also the base of 125; outliers 10 and 125 sit off the run.

21.why: 100 is the derivational hub of the whole set: 50, 25, 20 and 10 are 100 divided by 2, 4, 5 and 10 respectively.

22.why: No arithmetic or geometric middle, no sum of two options, no hub; 31/34/35 cluster against 12/18 with nothing to separate them.

23.why: 144 touches every other value (144=72x2=24x6=1728/12=2x72), but 1728=24x72 makes a competing product relation, so the hub is not clean.

24.why: Nothing distinguishes 15, 4, 8, 20, 9 - no sum, no run, no hub, and two perfect squares - so this is an unforced guess.
